title: Beyond Relevance: An Empirical Study of Multimodal LLMs for Diversity-Aware Recommendation Reranking
abstract: arXiv:2611.28379v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) have emerged as promising rerankers for recommendation, yet most existing approaches rely on textual item descriptions and primarily focus on relevance. In visually oriented domains such as video streaming, item images provide complementary signals that may also inform recommendation diversity. This raises two questions: when does visual information improve recommendation quality, and can multimodal LLMs (MLLMs) enhance relevance and diversity simultaneously? We investigate these questions through a training-free, diversity-aware multimodal reranking framework that jointly incorporates item images, textual metadata, and user interaction histories. We conduct an empirical study across three public Amazon Review datasets and an industrial Amazon Prime Video dataset, using both open-source and proprietary MLLMs. Our results reveal substantial domain-dependent effects: adding visual information yields up to 121.9

translated_title: 超越相关性：多模态大语言模型用于多样性感知推荐重排序的实证研究
translated_abstract: 大语言模型（LLM）已成为推荐系统中颇具前景的重排序器，然而大多数现有方法依赖于文本形式的物品描述，并主要关注相关性。在以视觉为导向的领域（如视频流媒体）中，物品图像提供了互补信号，这些信号也可能有助于提升推荐多样性。这引出了两个问题：视觉信息何时能提升推荐质量？多模态大语言模型（MLLM）能否同时增强相关性与多样性？我们通过一个无需训练的、多样性感知的多模态重排序框架来研究这些问题，该框架联合融入了物品图像、文本元数据和用户交互历史。我们在三个公开的亚马逊评论数据集和一个工业界的亚马逊Prime Video数据集上，使用开源与专有的多模态大语言模型开展了实证研究。我们的结果揭示了显著的领域依赖性效应：加入视觉信息最高可带来121.9%（原文此处截断）。
tldr: 本文提出一个无需训练的多样性感知多模态重排序框架，通过整合物品图像、文本元数据与用户交互历史，实证表明多模态大语言模型能够同时提升推荐的相关性与多样性，且视觉信息带来的增益具有明显的领域依赖性。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes a training-free, diversity-aware multimodal reranking framework that jointly leverages item images, textual metadata, and user interaction histories, empirically demonstrating that multimodal LLMs can improve both relevance and diversity in recommendation, with visual information yielding domain-dependent gains.
